memories.memory: I was diagnosed with high blood pressure in my early sixties and now take 10 mg of lisinopril each morning.
After a bone-density scan in February 2024 showed osteopenia in my hips, my doctor recommended vitamin D, calcium, and weight-bearing exercise instead of medication for now.
I had a minor cataract procedure on my right eye in October 2023, and I still use prescription reading glasses when I work at the computer.
My fasting blood sugar has been slightly elevated for the past two years, so my primary-care doctor is monitoring me for prediabetes rather than prescribing medication.
I went through several months of insomnia after my sister died, and a short course of counseling helped more than the sleeping pills I was initially offered.
A fall on an icy driveway last winter left me with a strained rotator cuff, and I completed eight weeks of physical therapy at a clinic near my home.
I have been putting off a colonoscopy because the preparation makes me anxious, although my doctor has reminded me that I am overdue for the screening.
